notes: Sourced from Autocue's own manufacturer datasheet PDF (hosted by pro-AV dealer CVP.com), which includes a high-resolution labeled rear-panel photo confirming exact port names/layout, plus a specs table (Controller Input: Serial; Video Outputs: 3x Composite (BNC), VGA, SDI (optional); Data Inputs: Ethernet, USB, PS2 keyboard; Power Input: 12V DC via 1x 4-pin XLR). An SDI video output is available as a factory-fit option but is not present on the standard unit shown in the labeled photo, so it was not added as a physical port. A small "WiFi" icon appears on the rear panel next to the composite outputs; this appears to be an integrated wireless module indicator rather than a discrete external-antenna port, so it was not added as a port. No connector id in the provided list matches a PS/2 mini-DIN keyboard jack; "midi-din" (closest DIN-family id) was used for the "Keyboard" port as an approximation — flag if a more precise id should be added. Neither Ethernet speed nor USB version is stated on this datasheet, so no "grade" was set on LAN/USB ports per instructions. This device is not rack-mountable (compact desktop chassis with a carry handle), so rackUnits was omitted. Category/type were approximated as source/"Media player" — QBox is technically a dedicated teleprompter "scroll engine" (receives script/control data, outputs prompter video), a niche function with no exact match in the provided type enum; "Control processor" is a plausible alternate type if a control-oriented classification is preferred. Note: Autocue later sold a redesigned "QBox V6" (per Markertek/CVP-independent retailer listings) with a different port set — 2x HD-SDI out, RJ45 in + RJ45 out, 2x USB2, 12V DC barrel-style aux input, and no VGA/composite/keyboard ports — this response covers the original "QBox Prompt Engine" pictured/labeled in the Autocue datasheet, not the V6 variant.
